# Add frame level operations to enhanced multi-frame instances

Add a `pydicom.multiframe` module, the same objects also reachable from `pydicom`, holding `frame_attributes(ds, index)`, `varying_attributes(ds)`, `extract_frames(ds, indices)`, `merge_frames(datasets)`, `group_frames(ds, keys)`, `sort_frames(ds, keys)` and `MultiFrameError`. All six reject the same malformed instances. `MultiFrameError`, a `ValueError`, is raised for a dataset with no per-frame groups, empty counting as none, transfer syntax, SOP class or instance UID, not exactly one pixel data element, a shared group sequence present but not holding one item, a frame count absent or disagreeing, pixel data too short or malformed, a missing frame, an empty or repeating selection, no keys, a key that is not an attribute name or tag, incomparable values, and uncombinable inputs.

`frame_attributes` returns the attributes in the macros applying to one zero-based frame, the shared macros written first and the frame's own second, a per-frame macro replacing the shared macro carrying its tag. It is a copy, so the instance is unaffected. `varying_attributes` returns the tags whose effective value is not the same for every frame, nothing for one frame.

`extract_frames` keeps the frames `indices` names, in order. `merge_frames` takes every frame of its inputs, one or more, which must agree on SOP class, transfer syntax, pixel data element and image pixel attributes. `group_frames` returns a list of one instance per distinct combination of the effective values of `keys`, in first-appearance order, keeping their old order, frames carrying none grouping together, even when that is every frame. `sort_frames` puts them in ascending order of those values, first key first, missing values last, ties as they were. Multi-valued attributes order value by value.

A derived instance carries one shared group. In-stack positions are renumbered from one within each stack, in frame order, among those carrying them. Among the frames carrying index values, described or not, a dimension every one of them reaches with one value is then dropped, from the dimension index description and from those frames; one they do not all reach is kept. A frame's values element goes when it empties, its macro stays; the description goes when nothing is left in it. What remains is renumbered, each alone, to 1, 2, 3 in first-seen order. Only then is a macro with the same value for every frame stored once, in the shared group, every other in each frame's own. A macro may hold several items. Its pixel data element is rebuilt in the new frame order, one-bit data packed and measured in bits, not bytes, encapsulated again if it was, its length left undefined, padded to an even length if not, any extended offset table dropped. It takes a new SOP instance UID, its file meta naming that and its SOP class, and a source image sequence holding one item per input, in input order, naming its SOP class, instance UID and the 1-based frame numbers taken from it, in result order. Whatever else it carries comes from the first input, copied. Inputs are unchanged and share nothing with the result.

Implemented `pydicom.multiframe` with all requested operations and `MultiFrameError`, exported from `pydicom`.

Includes strict validation, functional-group handling, dimension/in-stack normalization, native/bit-packed/encapsulated pixel rebuilding, UID/source-image updates, grouping, sorting, and merging.

Verification: 792 focused tests passed; full suite reached 2,633 passed with one unrelated TLS certificate failure during test-data download.

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /app/src/pydicom/multiframe.py
+# Copyright 2008-2025 pydicom authors. See LICENSE file for details.
+"""Operations on enhanced multi-frame image instances.
+
+The functions in this module deliberately operate on the encoded pixel data
+and on the functional groups rather than on ``Dataset.pixel_array``.  This
+means that selecting or re-ordering frames does not require a decoder (and
+also means that a compressed instance remains compressed).
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping, MutableSequence
+from copy import deepcopy
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from functools import cmp_to_key
+from numbers import Integral
+from struct import unpack_from
+from typing import Any, cast
+
+from pydicom.dataelem import DataElement
+from pydicom.datadict import dictionary_VR, tag_for_keyword
+from pydicom.dataset import Dataset
+from pydicom.encaps import encapsulate
+from pydicom.pixels.utils import pack_bits
+from pydicom.sequence import Sequence
+from pydicom.tag import BaseTag, Tag
+from pydicom.uid import UID, generate_uid
+from pydicom.valuerep import VR
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "MultiFrameError",
+    "extract_frames",
+    "frame_attributes",
+    "group_frames",
+    "merge_frames",
+    "sort_frames",
+    "varying_attributes",
+]
+
+
+class MultiFrameError(ValueError):
+    """Raised when an enhanced multi-frame instance cannot be operated on."""
+
+
+# Functional groups and pixel data tags
+_SHARED_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS = Tag(0x52009229)
+_PER_FRAME_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS = Tag(0x52009230)
+_DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE = Tag(0x00209222)
+_DIMENSION_INDEX_VALUES = Tag(0x00209157)
+_FRAME_CONTENT_SEQUENCE = Tag(0x00209111)
+_IN_STACK_POSITION_NUMBER = Tag(0x00209057)
+_STACK_ID = Tag(0x00209056)
+_NUMBER_OF_FRAMES = Tag(0x00280008)
+_PIXEL_DATA_TAGS = (
+    Tag(0x7FE00010),  # Pixel Data
+    Tag(0x7FE00008),  # Float Pixel Data
+    Tag(0x7FE00009),  # Double Float Pixel Data
+)
+_EXTENDED_OFFSET_TABLE = Tag(0x7FE00001)
+_EXTENDED_OFFSET_TABLE_LENGTHS = Tag(0x7FE00002)
+_SOURCE_IMAGE_SEQUENCE = Tag(0x00082112)
+
+# Image Pixel module elements.  The full set of present group 0028 elements is
+# compared for merging below; this set is used for the values needed to check
+# native pixel data length.
+_SAMPLES_PER_PIXEL = Tag(0x00280002)
+_ROWS = Tag(0x00280010)
+_COLUMNS = Tag(0x00280011)
+_BITS_ALLOCATED = Tag(0x00280100)
+_PHOTOMETRIC_INTERPRETATION = Tag(0x00280004)
+_PLANAR_CONFIGURATION = Tag(0x00280006)
+
+_MISSING = object()
+
+
+@dataclass
+class _FrameInfo:
+    """Validated information about one source instance."""
+
+    dataset: Dataset
+    transfer_syntax: UID
+    pixel_tag: BaseTag
+    pixel_element: DataElement
+    number_of_frames: int
+    shared: Dataset | None
+    per_frame: list[Dataset]
+    image_pixel: dict[BaseTag, Any]
+    samples_per_pixel: int
+    rows: int
+    columns: int
+    bits_allocated: int
+    frame_bits: int
+    pixel_data: bytes
+    encapsulated_frames: list[bytes] | None
+
+
+def _fail(message: str) -> None:
+    raise MultiFrameError(message)
+
+
+def _as_bytes(value: Any, what: str) -> bytes:
+    """Return a byte value or raise the public error type."""
+
+    if isinstance(value, bytes):
+        return value
+    if isinstance(value, bytearray):
+        return bytes(value)
+    if isinstance(value, memoryview):
+        return value.tobytes()
+    _fail(f"The {what} is not a byte value")
+
+
+def _uid(value: Any, what: str, *, transfer_syntax: bool = False) -> UID:
+    if value is None or value == "":
+        _fail(f"The {what} is absent or empty")
+
+    try:
+        result = value if isinstance(value, UID) else UID(str(value))
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"The {what} is invalid") from exc
+
+    if not result:
+        _fail(f"The {what} is absent or empty")
+    if transfer_syntax:
+        try:
+            valid = result.is_transfer_syntax
+        except Exception:
+            valid = False
+        if not valid:
+            _fail("The Transfer Syntax UID is invalid")
+
+    return result
+
+
+def _integer(value: Any, what: str) -> int:
+    if isinstance(value, bool):
+        _fail(f"The {what} is invalid")
+
+    try:
+        result = int(value)
+    except (TypeError, ValueError, OverflowError) as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"The {what} is invalid") from exc
+
+    # Do not silently turn a fractional float into a valid integer.
+    if isinstance(value, float) and value != result:
+        _fail(f"The {what} is invalid")
+    if result <= 0:
+        _fail(f"The {what} is invalid")
+    return result
+
+
+def _element(ds: Dataset, tag: BaseTag) -> DataElement | None:
+    """Get an element without relying on Dataset's keyword conversion."""
+
+    try:
+        value = ds._dict.get(tag)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The dataset is malformed") from exc
+
+    if value is None:
+        return None
+    if not isinstance(value, DataElement):
+        # Accessing a RawDataElement converts it in normal pydicom use.  A raw
+        # element left in a hand-built Dataset is still best handled through
+        # Dataset.__getitem__ so that the public API behaves as usual.
+        try:
+            value = ds[tag]
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError(f"The element {tag} is malformed") from exc
+    return cast(DataElement, value)
+
+
+def _sequence_items(
+    ds: Dataset, tag: BaseTag, *, required: bool = False, one: bool = False
+) -> list[Dataset] | None:
+    elem = _element(ds, tag)
+    if elem is None:
+        if required:
+            _fail(f"The required sequence {tag} is absent")
+        return None
+
+    if elem.VR != VR.SQ:
+        _fail(f"The sequence {tag} is malformed")
+
+    try:
+        value = elem.value
+        items = list(value)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"The sequence {tag} is malformed") from exc
+
+    if any(not isinstance(item, Dataset) for item in items):
+        _fail(f"The sequence {tag} contains a non-dataset item")
+    if one and len(items) != 1:
+        _fail(f"The sequence {tag} must contain exactly one item")
+    if required and not items:
+        _fail(f"The required sequence {tag} is empty")
+    return cast(list[Dataset], items)
+
+
+def _image_pixel_attributes(ds: Dataset) -> dict[BaseTag, Any]:
+    """Return all present Image Pixel group values except Number of Frames."""
+
+    result: dict[BaseTag, Any] = {}
+    for tag, elem in ds._dict.items():
+        tag = BaseTag(tag)
+        if tag.group == 0x0028 and tag != _NUMBER_OF_FRAMES:
+            try:
+                result[tag] = deepcopy(ds[tag].value)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                raise MultiFrameError(f"The image pixel attribute {tag} is malformed") from exc
+    return result
+
+
+def _native_pixel_length(info: _FrameInfo) -> None:
+    """Validate the length and padding of a native pixel data value."""
+
+    expected_bytes = (info.number_of_frames * info.frame_bits + 7) // 8
+    actual = len(info.pixel_data)
+
+    # A native Pixel Data value is even length.  The only permissible excess
+    # is the single pad byte required when the unpadded value is odd.
+    permitted = expected_bytes + (expected_bytes % 2)
+    if actual < expected_bytes or actual > permitted or actual % 2:
+        _fail("The native pixel data is too short or malformed")
+
+
+def _unpack_u64_values(value: Any, what: str) -> list[int]:
+    raw = _as_bytes(value, what)
+    if len(raw) % 8:
+        _fail(f"The {what} is malformed")
+    try:
+        return list(unpack_from(f"<{len(raw) // 8}Q", raw)) if raw else []
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"The {what} is malformed") from exc
+
+
+def _encapsulated_frames(
+    data: bytes,
+    number_of_frames: int,
+    extended_offsets: tuple[Any, Any] | None,
+) -> list[bytes]:
+    """Parse an encapsulated Pixel Data value strictly.
+
+    The general-purpose helpers in :mod:`pydicom.encaps` intentionally accept
+    some damaged data and issue warnings.  Multi-frame transformations need a
+    deterministic frame boundary, so this parser verifies the item and
+    delimiter structure before forming the frames.
+    """
+
+    if len(data) < 8:
+        _fail("The encapsulated pixel data is too short or malformed")
+
+    # Encapsulation item tags and lengths are little endian, independent of the
+    # transfer syntax used for the compressed codestream.
+    if data[0:4] != b"\xfe\xff\x00\xe0":
+        _fail("The encapsulated pixel data is malformed")
+    bot_length = int.from_bytes(data[4:8], "little")
+    bot_end = 8 + bot_length
+    if bot_end > len(data) or bot_length % 4:
+        _fail("The Basic Offset Table is malformed")
+    bot = [
+        int.from_bytes(data[offset : offset + 4], "little")
+        for offset in range(8, bot_end, 4)
+    ]
+
+    fragment_starts: list[int] = []
+    fragments: list[bytes] = []
+    offset = bot_end
+    delimiter_end: int | None = None
+    while offset < len(data):
+        if offset + 8 > len(data):
+            _fail("The encapsulated pixel data is truncated")
+        tag = data[offset : offset + 4]
+        length = int.from_bytes(data[offset + 4 : offset + 8], "little")
+        if tag == b"\xfe\xff\x00\xe0":
+            if length == 0xFFFFFFFF or offset + 8 + length > len(data):
+                _fail("An encapsulated pixel data fragment is malformed")
+            fragment_starts.append(offset - bot_end)
+            fragments.append(data[offset + 8 : offset + 8 + length])
+            offset += 8 + length
+            continue
+        if tag == b"\xfe\xff\xdd\xe0":
+            if length != 0:
+                _fail("The encapsulated pixel data delimiter is malformed")
+            delimiter_end = offset + 8
+            break
+        _fail("The encapsulated pixel data contains an unexpected item")
+
+    if delimiter_end is None or delimiter_end != len(data):
+        _fail("The encapsulated pixel data is missing its delimiter")
+    if not fragments or any(not fragment for fragment in fragments):
+        _fail("The encapsulated pixel data contains a missing frame")
+
+    # Extended Offset Table values, when present, describe one fragment per
+    # frame.  Both elements are required together.
+    if extended_offsets is not None:
+        offsets = _unpack_u64_values(extended_offsets[0], "Extended Offset Table")
+        lengths = _unpack_u64_values(
+            extended_offsets[1], "Extended Offset Table Lengths"
+        )
+        if len(offsets) != number_of_frames or len(lengths) != number_of_frames:
+            _fail("The Extended Offset Table does not describe every frame")
+        out: list[bytes] = []
+        for frame_offset, frame_length in zip(offsets, lengths):
+            if frame_offset not in fragment_starts:
+                _fail("The Extended Offset Table is malformed")
+            position = fragment_starts.index(frame_offset)
+            if position >= len(fragments):
+                _fail("The Extended Offset Table is malformed")
+            if frame_length != len(fragments[position]):
+                _fail("The Extended Offset Table Lengths are malformed")
+            out.append(fragments[position])
+        if len(set(offsets)) != len(offsets):
+            _fail("The Extended Offset Table is malformed")
+        return out
+
+    if bot:
+        if len(bot) != number_of_frames:
+            _fail("The Basic Offset Table does not describe every frame")
+        if any(value not in fragment_starts for value in bot):
+            _fail("The Basic Offset Table is malformed")
+        if len(set(bot)) != len(bot):
+            _fail("The Basic Offset Table is malformed")
+
+        starts = [fragment_starts.index(value) for value in bot]
+        if starts != sorted(starts) or starts[0] != 0:
+            _fail("The Basic Offset Table is malformed")
+        frames: list[bytes] = []
+        for index, start in enumerate(starts):
+            stop = starts[index + 1] if index + 1 < len(starts) else len(fragments)
+            if stop <= start:
+                _fail("The Basic Offset Table is malformed")
+            frames.append(b"".join(fragments[start:stop]))
+        return frames
+
+    # Without either offset table, one fragment per frame is unambiguous.  A
+    # single frame may contain any number of fragments.
+    if len(fragments) == number_of_frames:
+        return fragments
+    if number_of_frames == 1:
+        return [b"".join(fragments)]
+
+    # JPEG-family codestreams are the only case where pydicom can infer frame
+    # boundaries from a no-offset-table stream with multiple fragments.
+    frames = []
+    current: list[bytes] = []
+    for fragment in fragments:
+        current.append(fragment)
+        if b"\xff\xd9" in fragment[-10:]:
+            frames.append(b"".join(current))
+            current = []
+    if current:
+        frames.append(b"".join(current))
+    if len(frames) != number_of_frames:
+        _fail("The encapsulated pixel data does not contain the expected frames")
+    return frames
+
+
+def _validate_dataset(ds: Dataset) -> _FrameInfo:
+    """Validate and collect all information shared by the public functions."""
+
+    if not isinstance(ds, Dataset):
+        _fail("The value is not a DICOM dataset")
+
+    try:
+        file_meta = ds.file_meta
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The dataset has no file meta information") from exc
+    if not isinstance(file_meta, Dataset):
+        _fail("The dataset has no file meta information")
+    transfer_syntax = _uid(
+        _element(file_meta, Tag(0x00020010)).value
+        if _element(file_meta, Tag(0x00020010)) is not None
+        else None,
+        "Transfer Syntax UID",
+        transfer_syntax=True,
+    )
+
+    sop_class_elem = _element(ds, Tag(0x00080016))
+    sop_instance_elem = _element(ds, Tag(0x00080018))
+    _uid(
+        sop_class_elem.value if sop_class_elem is not None else None,
+        "SOP Class UID",
+    )
+    _uid(
+        sop_instance_elem.value if sop_instance_elem is not None else None,
+        "SOP Instance UID",
+    )
+
+    shared_items = _sequence_items(ds, _SHARED_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS, one=True)
+    shared = shared_items[0] if shared_items else None
+    per_frame = _sequence_items(ds, _PER_FRAME_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS, required=True)
+    assert per_frame is not None
+
+    number_elem = _element(ds, _NUMBER_OF_FRAMES)
+    if number_elem is None:
+        _fail("Number of Frames is absent")
+    number_of_frames = _integer(number_elem.value, "Number of Frames")
+    if len(per_frame) != number_of_frames:
+        _fail("Number of Frames disagrees with the per-frame groups")
+
+    pixel_elements: list[tuple[BaseTag, DataElement]] = []
+    for tag in _PIXEL_DATA_TAGS:
+        elem = _element(ds, tag)
+        if elem is not None:
+            pixel_elements.append((tag, elem))
+    if len(pixel_elements) != 1:
+        _fail("The dataset must contain exactly one pixel data element")
+    pixel_tag, pixel_element = pixel_elements[0]
+    pixel_data = _as_bytes(pixel_element.value, "pixel data")
+
+    # Required values for determining native frame boundaries.  These are also
+    # the values which are needed to concatenate one-bit frames correctly.
+    samples_elem = _element(ds, _SAMPLES_PER_PIXEL)
+    rows_elem = _element(ds, _ROWS)
+    columns_elem = _element(ds, _COLUMNS)
+    if samples_elem is None or rows_elem is None or columns_elem is None:
+        _fail("The image pixel attributes needed for frame length are absent")
+    samples_per_pixel = _integer(samples_elem.value, "Samples per Pixel")
+    rows = _integer(rows_elem.value, "Rows")
+    columns = _integer(columns_elem.value, "Columns")
+
+    if pixel_tag == _PIXEL_DATA_TAGS[1]:
+        bits_allocated = 32
+        if not transfer_syntax.is_encapsulated and pixel_element.VR != VR.OF:
+            _fail("Float Pixel Data is malformed")
+    elif pixel_tag == _PIXEL_DATA_TAGS[2]:
+        bits_allocated = 64
+        if not transfer_syntax.is_encapsulated and pixel_element.VR != VR.OD:
+            _fail("Double Float Pixel Data is malformed")
+    else:
+        bits_elem = _element(ds, _BITS_ALLOCATED)
+        if bits_elem is None:
+            _fail("Bits Allocated is absent")
+        bits_allocated = _integer(bits_elem.value, "Bits Allocated")
+        if bits_allocated != 1 and bits_allocated % 8:
+            _fail("Bits Allocated is malformed")
+
+    frame_bits = samples_per_pixel * rows * columns * bits_allocated
+    if frame_bits <= 0:
+        _fail("The image pixel attributes are malformed")
+
+    encapsulated_frames: list[bytes] | None = None
+    if transfer_syntax.is_encapsulated:
+        if pixel_tag != _PIXEL_DATA_TAGS[0] or pixel_element.VR != VR.OB:
+            _fail("The encapsulated pixel data element is malformed")
+
+        eot_elem = _element(ds, _EXTENDED_OFFSET_TABLE)
+        eotl_elem = _element(ds, _EXTENDED_OFFSET_TABLE_LENGTHS)
+        if (eot_elem is None) != (eotl_elem is None):
+            _fail("The Extended Offset Table is incomplete")
+        extended_offsets = (
+            (eot_elem.value, eotl_elem.value)
+            if eot_elem is not None and eotl_elem is not None
+            else None
+        )
+        encapsulated_frames = _encapsulated_frames(
+            pixel_data, number_of_frames, extended_offsets
+        )
+        if len(encapsulated_frames) != number_of_frames:
+            _fail("The encapsulated pixel data has the wrong number of frames")
+    else:
+        if pixel_element.is_undefined_length:
+            _fail("Native pixel data must have a defined length")
+        _native_info = _FrameInfo(
+            ds,
+            transfer_syntax,
+            pixel_tag,
+            pixel_element,
+            number_of_frames,
+            shared,
+            per_frame,
+            {},
+            samples_per_pixel,
+            rows,
+            columns,
+            bits_allocated,
+            frame_bits,
+            pixel_data,
+            None,
+        )
+        _native_pixel_length(_native_info)
+
+    return _FrameInfo(
+        ds,
+        transfer_syntax,
+        pixel_tag,
+        pixel_element,
+        number_of_frames,
+        shared,
+        per_frame,
+        _image_pixel_attributes(ds),
+        samples_per_pixel,
+        rows,
+        columns,
+        bits_allocated,
+        frame_bits,
+        pixel_data,
+        encapsulated_frames,
+    )
+
+
+def _effective_attributes(info: _FrameInfo, index: int) -> Dataset:
+    """Return a deep copy of the effective functional-group item."""
+
+    if not isinstance(index, Integral) or isinstance(index, bool):
+        _fail("The frame index is invalid")
+    index = int(index)
+    if index < 0 or index >= info.number_of_frames:
+        _fail(f"Frame index {index} is missing")
+
+    result = Dataset()
+    if info.shared is not None:
+        for tag, elem in info.shared.items():
+            result[BaseTag(tag)] = deepcopy(elem)
+    for tag, elem in info.per_frame[index].items():
+        result[BaseTag(tag)] = deepcopy(elem)
+    return result
+
+
+def frame_attributes(ds: Dataset, index: int) -> Dataset:
+    """Return the effective functional-group macros for one frame.
+
+    ``index`` is zero based.  The returned :class:`~pydicom.dataset.Dataset`
+    is independent of ``ds``.
+    """
+
+    info = _validate_dataset(ds)
+    return _effective_attributes(info, index)
+
+
+def _values_equal(left: Any, right: Any) -> bool:
+    """Compare DICOM values without leaking array truth-value errors."""
+
+    if left is right:
+        return True
+    if isinstance(left, Dataset) and isinstance(right, Dataset):
+        try:
+            return bool(left == right)
+        except Exception:
+            return False
+    if isinstance(left, (list, tuple, MutableSequence)) and isinstance(
+        right, (list, tuple, MutableSequence)
+    ):
+        if len(left) != len(right):
+            return False
+        return all(_values_equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(left, right))
+    try:
+        result = left == right
+        return bool(result)
+    except Exception:
+        return False
+
+
+def varying_attributes(ds: Dataset) -> set[BaseTag]:
+    """Return functional-group macro tags whose effective value varies."""
+
+    info = _validate_dataset(ds)
+    if info.number_of_frames == 1:
+        return set()
+
+    frames = [_effective_attributes(info, index) for index in range(info.number_of_frames)]
+    tags: set[BaseTag] = set()
+    all_tags = set().union(*(set(frame._dict) for frame in frames))
+    for tag in all_tags:
+        first = frames[0]._dict.get(tag, _MISSING)
+        if any(
+            not _values_equal(
+                first,
+                frame._dict.get(tag, _MISSING),
+            )
+            for frame in frames[1:]
+        ):
+            tags.add(BaseTag(tag))
+    return tags
+
+
+def _normalise_key(key: Any) -> BaseTag:
+    if isinstance(key, str):
+        tag = tag_for_keyword(key)
+        if tag is None:
+            _fail(f"'{key}' is not a DICOM attribute name or tag")
+        return Tag(tag)
+    try:
+        return Tag(key)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError(f"'{key}' is not a DICOM attribute name or tag") from exc
+
+
+def _keys(keys: Any) -> list[BaseTag]:
+    if isinstance(keys, (str, BaseTag, Integral)):
+        raw_keys = [keys]
+    elif isinstance(keys, tuple) and len(keys) == 2 and all(
+        isinstance(value, Integral) for value in keys
+    ):
+        raw_keys = [keys]
+    else:
+        try:
+            raw_keys = list(keys)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("The keys are invalid") from exc
+    if not raw_keys:
+        _fail("At least one key is required")
+    return [_normalise_key(key) for key in raw_keys]
+
+
+def _iter_nested_values(ds: Dataset, tag: BaseTag) -> list[Any]:
+    """Find direct attributes with ``tag`` inside functional-group macros."""
+
+    values: list[Any] = []
+
+    def visit(node: Dataset) -> None:
+        for elem_tag, elem in node.items():
+            if BaseTag(elem_tag) == tag:
+                values.append(elem.value)
+            if elem.VR == VR.SQ:
+                try:
+                    items = elem.value
+                    for item in items:
+                        if isinstance(item, Dataset):
+                            visit(item)
+                except Exception as exc:
+                    raise MultiFrameError("A functional-group macro is malformed") from exc
+
+    visit(ds)
+    return values
+
+
+def _key_value(frame: Dataset, key: BaseTag) -> Any:
+    # A macro sequence itself is a useful key and is the direct interpretation
+    # of a key that names one of the attributes returned by frame_attributes().
+    elem = _element(frame, key)
+    if elem is not None:
+        value = elem.value
+        return _MISSING if value is None else value
+
+    values = _iter_nested_values(frame, key)
+    if values:
+        if len(values) == 1:
+            return _MISSING if values[0] is None else values[0]
+        return tuple(values)
+    return _MISSING
+
+
+def _components(value: Any) -> tuple[Any, ...]:
+    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, MutableSequence)) and not isinstance(
+        value, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)
+    ):
+        return tuple(value)
+    return (value,)
+
+
+def _compare_atomic(left: Any, right: Any) -> int:
+    if _values_equal(left, right):
+        return 0
+    try:
+        if left < right:
+            return -1
+        if left > right:
+            return 1
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("Frame attribute values are incomparable") from exc
+    raise MultiFrameError("Frame attribute values are incomparable")
+
+
+def _compare_values(left: Any, right: Any) -> int:
+    left_parts = _components(left)
+    right_parts = _components(right)
+    for left_part, right_part in zip(left_parts, right_parts):
+        result = _compare_atomic(left_part, right_part)
+        if result:
+            return result
+    if len(left_parts) < len(right_parts):
+        return -1
+    if len(left_parts) > len(right_parts):
+        return 1
+    return 0
+
+
+def _frame_key_values(
+    info: _FrameInfo, keys: list[BaseTag]
+) -> tuple[list[Dataset], list[tuple[Any, ...]]]:
+    frames = [_effective_attributes(info, index) for index in range(info.number_of_frames)]
+    values = [tuple(_key_value(frame, key) for key in keys) for frame in frames]
+    return frames, values
+
+
+def _validate_comparable(values: list[tuple[Any, ...]]) -> None:
+    for key_index in range(len(values[0])):
+        present = [value[key_index] for value in values if value[key_index] is not _MISSING]
+        for left_index, left in enumerate(present):
+            for right in present[left_index + 1 :]:
+                _compare_values(left, right)
+
+
+def _combination_equal(
+    left: tuple[Any, ...], right: tuple[Any, ...]
+) -> bool:
+    for left_value, right_value in zip(left, right):
+        if left_value is _MISSING or right_value is _MISSING:
+            if left_value is not right_value:
+                return False
+            continue
+        if _compare_values(left_value, right_value) != 0:
+            return False
+    return True
+
+
+def _normalise_indices(indices: Iterable[int], number_of_frames: int) -> list[int]:
+    if isinstance(indices, (str, bytes, bytearray)):
+        _fail("The frame selection is invalid")
+    try:
+        result = list(indices)
+    except Exception as exc:
+        raise MultiFrameError("The frame selection is invalid") from exc
+    if not result:
+        _fail("The frame selection is empty")
+    if any(not isinstance(index, Integral) or isinstance(index, bool) for index in result):
+        _fail("The frame selection contains an invalid frame index")
+    result = [int(index) for index in result]
+    if len(set(result)) != len(result):
+        _fail("The frame selection repeats a frame")
+    if any(index < 0 or index >= number_of_frames for index in result):
+        _fail("The frame selection contains a missing frame")
+    return result
+
+
+def _stack_value(frame: Dataset) -> Any:
+    content = _element(frame, _FRAME_CONTENT_SEQUENCE)
+    if content is None or content.VR != VR.SQ:
+        return _MISSING
+    values = []
+    for item in content.value:
+        if isinstance(item, Dataset):
+            elem = _element(item, _STACK_ID)
+            if elem is not None and elem.value is not None:
+                values.append(elem.value)
+    if not values:
+        return _MISSING
+    return values[0] if len(values) == 1 else tuple(values)
+
+
+def _frame_content_items(frame: Dataset) -> list[Dataset]:
+    content = _element(frame, _FRAME_CONTENT_SEQUENCE)
+    if content is None:
+        return []
+    if content.VR != VR.SQ:
+        _fail("A Frame Content Sequence macro is malformed")
+    items = list(content.value)
+    if any(not isinstance(item, Dataset) for item in items):
+        _fail("A Frame Content Sequence macro is malformed")
+    return cast(list[Dataset], items)
+
+
+def _renumber_in_stack(frames: list[Dataset]) -> None:
+    counters: list[tuple[Any, int]] = []
+    for frame in frames:
+        items = _frame_content_items(frame)
+        if not any(_element(item, _IN_STACK_POSITION_NUMBER) is not None for item in items):
+            continue
+        stack = _stack_value(frame)
+        counter = None
+        for old_stack, old_counter in counters:
+            if (stack is _MISSING and old_stack is _MISSING) or (
+                stack is not _MISSING
+                and old_stack is not _MISSING
+                and _values_equal(stack, old_stack)
+            ):
+                counter = old_counter + 1
+                counters[counters.index((old_stack, old_counter))] = (old_stack, counter)
+                break
+        if counter is None:
+            counter = 1
+            counters.append((stack, counter))
+        for item in items:
+            elem = _element(item, _IN_STACK_POSITION_NUMBER)
+            if elem is not None:
+                elem.value = counter
+
+
+def _dimension_values(frame: Dataset) -> tuple[Dataset | None, list[Any] | None]:
+    items = _frame_content_items(frame)
+    for item in items:
+        elem = _element(item, _DIMENSION_INDEX_VALUES)
+        if elem is not None:
+            value = elem.value
+            if value is None:
+                return item, []
+            if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, MutableSequence)):
+                return item, list(value)
+            return item, [value]
+    return None, None
+
+
+def _renumber_dimensions(frames: list[Dataset], output: Dataset) -> None:
+    """Drop constant dimensions and renumber every remaining dimension."""
+
+    descriptions_elem = _element(output, _DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE)
+    descriptions: list[Dataset] = []
+    if descriptions_elem is not None:
+        if descriptions_elem.VR != VR.SQ:
+            _fail("The Dimension Index Sequence is malformed")
+        descriptions = list(descriptions_elem.value)
+        if any(not isinstance(item, Dataset) for item in descriptions):
+            _fail("The Dimension Index Sequence is malformed")
+
+    values_by_frame: list[list[Any] | None] = []
+    value_items: list[Dataset | None] = []
+    for frame in frames:
+        item, values = _dimension_values(frame)
+        value_items.append(item)
+        values_by_frame.append(values)
+
+    carrying = [values for values in values_by_frame if values]
+    if not carrying:
+        # There are no values to transform.  Keep a description if one was
+        # supplied; it still describes the instance, even if this selection
+        # carries no frame values.
+        return
+
+    max_dimensions = max(
+        [len(values) for values in carrying] + [len(descriptions)]
+    )
+    dropped: set[int] = set()
+    for dimension in range(max_dimensions):
+        reached = [values for values in carrying if len(values) > dimension]
+        if len(reached) == len(carrying) and reached:
+            first = reached[0][dimension]
+            if all(_values_equal(first, values[dimension]) for values in reached[1:]):
+                dropped.add(dimension)
+
+    kept = [dimension for dimension in range(max_dimensions) if dimension not in dropped]
+    first_seen: dict[int, list[Any]] = {dimension: [] for dimension in kept}
+    for values in values_by_frame:
+        if not values:
+            continue
+        new_values: list[Any] = []
+        for dimension in kept:
+            if dimension >= len(values):
+                continue
+            value = values[dimension]
+            seen = first_seen[dimension]
+            match = next((old for old in seen if _values_equal(old, value)), _MISSING)
+            if match is _MISSING:
+                seen.append(value)
+                new_values.append(len(seen))
+            else:
+                new_values.append(seen.index(match) + 1)
+
+        item = value_items[values_by_frame.index(values)] if False else None
+        # The index lookup above would be ambiguous for repeated lists; update
+        # items in a second indexed pass below instead.
+
+    for frame_index, (frame, values, item) in enumerate(
+        zip(frames, values_by_frame, value_items)
+    ):
+        if not values or item is None:
+            continue
+        new_values = []
+        for dimension in kept:
+            if dimension >= len(values):
+                continue
+            value = values[dimension]
+            seen = first_seen[dimension]
+            match_index = next(
+                (index for index, old in enumerate(seen) if _values_equal(old, value)),
+                None,
+            )
+            if match_index is None:
+                # This can only occur for a value not encountered in the first
+                # pass, which is defensive support for unusual mutable values.
+                seen.append(value)
+                match_index = len(seen) - 1
+            new_values.append(match_index + 1)
+
+        elem = _element(item, _DIMENSION_INDEX_VALUES)
+        if not new_values:
+            if elem is not None:
+                del item[_DIMENSION_INDEX_VALUES]
+        elif elem is not None:
+            elem.value = new_values
+
+    if descriptions:
+        remaining_descriptions = [
+            deepcopy(description)
+            for index, description in enumerate(descriptions)
+            if index not in dropped
+        ]
+        if remaining_descriptions:
+            output[_DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE] = DataElement(
+                _DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE,
+                descriptions_elem.VR if descriptions_elem is not None else VR.SQ,
+                Sequence(remaining_descriptions),
+            )
+        else:
+            del output[_DIMENSION_INDEX_SEQUENCE]
+
+
+def _split_functional_groups(frames: list[Dataset]) -> tuple[Dataset, list[Dataset]]:
+    all_tags: set[BaseTag] = set().union(*(set(frame._dict) for frame in frames))
+    shared = Dataset()
+    per_frame = [Dataset() for _ in frames]
+    for tag in all_tags:
+        present = [frame._dict.get(tag, _MISSING) for frame in frames]
+        if all(value is not _MISSING for value in present) and all(
+            _values_equal(present[0], value) for value in present[1:]
+        ):
+            shared[BaseTag(tag)] = deepcopy(cast(DataElement, present[0]))
+            continue
+        for frame, value in zip(per_frame, present):
+            if value is not _MISSING:
+                frame[BaseTag(tag)] = deepcopy(cast(DataElement, value))
+    return shared, per_frame
+
+
+def _source_image_sequence(
+    selections: list[tuple[Dataset, list[int]]], output: Dataset
+) -> Sequence:
+    result = Sequence()
+    for source, indices in selections:
+        item = Dataset()
+        item.ReferencedSOPClassUID = deepcopy(source.SOPClassUID)
+        item.ReferencedSOPInstanceUID = deepcopy(source.SOPInstanceUID)
+        item.ReferencedFrameNumber = [index + 1 for index in indices]
+        result.append(item)
+    return result
+
+
+def _pixel_output(
+    infos: list[_FrameInfo], selections: list[tuple[_FrameInfo, list[int]]]
+) -> bytes:
+    first = infos[0]
+    if first.encapsulated_frames is not None:
+        frames: list[bytes] = []
+        for info, indices in selections:
+            assert info.encapsulated_frames is not None
+            frames.extend(info.encapsulated_frames[index] for index in indices)
+        try:
+            return encapsulate(frames)
+        except Exception as exc:
+            raise MultiFrameError("The selected pixel data cannot be encapsulated") from exc
+
+    if first.bits_allocated == 1:
+        total_pixels = first.frame_bits  # one bit per pixel when Bits Allocated = 1
+        unpacked = bytearray()
+        for info, indices in selections:
+            source = info.pixel_data
+            # The final native pad byte is deliberately left out of the bit
+            # stream.  Frame boundaries are measured in bits, not bytes.
+            bits = bytearray()
+            for value in source:
+                for bit in range(8):
+                    bits.append((value >> bit) & 1)
+            for index in indices:
+                start = index * total_pixels
+                unpacked.extend(bits[start : start + total_pixels])
+        return pack_bits(bytes(unpacked), pad=True)
+
+    bytes_per_frame = first.frame_bits // 8
+    output = bytearray()
+    for info, indices in selections:
+        source = info.pixel_data[: info.number_of_frames * bytes_per_frame]
+        for index in indices:
+            start = index * bytes_per_frame
+            output.extend(source[start : start + bytes_per_frame])
+    if len(output) % 2:
+        output.append(0)
+    return bytes(output)
+
+
+def _derive(
+    selections: list[tuple[Dataset, _FrameInfo, list[int]]],
+) -> Dataset:
+    first_source, first_info, _ = selections[0]
+    result = deepcopy(first_source)
+
+    effective: list[Dataset] = []
+    source_selections: list[tuple[Dataset, list[int]]] = []
+    pixel_selections: list[tuple[_FrameInfo, list[int]]] = []
+    infos: list[_FrameInfo] = []
+    for source, info, indices in selections:
+        infos.append(info)
+        source_selections.append((source, indices))
+        pixel_selections.append((info, indices))
+        effective.extend(_effective_attributes(info, index) for index in indices)
+
+    _renumber_in_stack(effective)
+    _renumber_dimensions(effective, result)
+    shared, per_frame = _split_functional_groups(effective)
+
+    result[_SHARED_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS] = DataElement(
+        _SHARED_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS, VR.SQ, Sequence([shared])
+    )
+    result[_PER_FRAME_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS] = DataElement(
+        _PER_FRAME_FUNCTIONAL_GROUPS, VR.SQ, Sequence(per_frame)
+    )
+    result.NumberOfFrames = len(effective)
+
+    # Rebuilding the pixel element also clears any old EOT values.  The basic
+    # offset table generated here is sufficient for the selected frames.
+    try:
+        result[first_info.pixel_tag].value = _pixel_output(infos, pixel_selections)
+    except MultiFrameError:

        :class:`int`.
    private_creator : str

    dataset : Dataset

        self.private_creator = key[1]
        self.dataset = dataset
        self.block_start = private_creator_element << 8

    def get_tag(self, element_offset: int) -> BaseTag:
        """Return the private tag ID for the given `element_offset`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag.

        Returns
        -------
            The tag ID defined by the private block location and the
            given element offset.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `element_offset` is too large.
        """
        if element_offset > 0xFF:
            raise ValueError("Element offset must be less than 256")
        return Tag(self.group, self.block_start + element_offset)

    def __contains__(self, element_offset: int) -> bool:
        """Return ``True`` if the tag with given `element_offset` is in
        the parent :class:`Dataset`.
        """
        return self.get_tag(element_offset) in self.dataset

    def __getitem__(self, element_offset: int) -> DataElement:
        """Return the data element in the parent dataset for the given element
        offset.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag.

        Returns
        -------
            The data element of the tag in the parent dataset defined by the
            private block location and the given element offset.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `element_offset` is too large.
        KeyError
            If no data element exists at that offset.
        """
        return self.dataset.__getitem__(self.get_tag(element_offset))

    def __delitem__(self, element_offset: int) -> None:
        """Delete the tag with the given `element_offset` from the dataset.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag
            to be deleted.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `element_offset` is too large.
        KeyError
            If no data element exists at that offset.
        """
        del self.dataset[self.get_tag(element_offset)]

    def add_new(self, element_offset: int, VR: str, value: object) -> None:
        """Add a private element to the parent :class:`Dataset`.

        Adds the private tag with the given `VR` and `value` to the parent
        :class:`Dataset` at the tag ID defined by the private block and the
        given `element_offset`.

        Parameters
        ----------
        element_offset : int
            The lower 16 bits (e.g. 2 hex numbers) of the element tag
            to be added.
        VR : str
            The 2 character DICOM value representation.
        value
            The value of the data element. See :meth:`Dataset.add_new()`
            for a description.
        """
        tag = self.get_tag(element_offset)
        self.dataset.add_new(tag, VR, value)
        self.dataset[tag].private_creator = self.private_creator


def _dict_equal(a: "Dataset", b: Any, exclude: list[str] | None = None) -> bool:
    """Common method for Dataset.__eq__ and FileDataset.__eq__

    Uses .keys() as needed because Dataset iter return items not keys
    `exclude` is used in FileDataset__eq__ ds.__dict__ compare, which
    would also compare the wrapped _dict member (entire dataset) again.
    """
    return (
        len(a) == len(b)
        and all(key in b for key in a.keys())
        and all(
            a[key] == b[key]
            for key in a.keys()
            if exclude is None or key not in exclude
        )
    )


_DatasetValue = DataElement | RawDataElement
_DatasetType: TypeAlias = "Dataset | MutableMapping[BaseTag, _DatasetValue]"

"""Functions for working with encapsulated (compressed) pixel data."""

from collections.abc import Iterator
from io import BytesIO, BufferedIOBase
import os
from struct import pack, unpack
from typing import Any

from pydicom import config
from pydicom.misc import warn_and_log
from pydicom.filebase import DicomBytesIO, DicomIO, ReadableBuffer
from pydicom.fileutil import buffer_length, reset_buffer_position
from pydicom.tag import Tag, ItemTag, SequenceDelimiterTag


# Functions for parsing encapsulated data
def parse_basic_offsets(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> list[int]:
    """Return the encapsulated pixel data's basic offset table frame offsets.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, positioned at the
        beginning of the Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`,
        :class:`bytearray` or an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and
        ``seek()`` methods. If the latter then after reading it will be
        positioned at the start of the item tag of the first fragment after the
        Basic Offset Table.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Returns
    -------
    list[int]
        A list of the offset positions to the first item tag of each frame, as
        measured from the end of the basic offset table.

    References
    ----------
    :dcm:`DICOM Standard, Part 5, Annex A.4<part05/sect_A.4.html#table_A.4-1>`
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
    if group << 16 | elem != 0xFFFEE000:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Found unexpected tag {Tag(group, elem)} instead of (FFFE,E000) "
            "when parsing the Basic Offset Table item"
        )

    length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", buffer.read(4))[0]
    if length % 4:
        raise ValueError(
            "The length of the Basic Offset Table item is not a multiple of 4"
        )

    if length == 0:
        return []

    return list(unpack(f"{endianness}{length // 4}L", buffer.read(length)))


def parse_fragments(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> tuple[int, list[int]]:
    """Return the number of fragments and their positions in `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, starting at the first
        byte of item tag for a fragment, such as after the end of the Basic
        Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray` or an
        object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and ``seek()`` methods. If the latter
        then the offset will be reset to the starting position afterwards.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[int, list[int]]
        The number of fragments and the absolute offset position of the first
        byte of the item tag for each fragment in `buffer`.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    start_offset = buffer.tell()

    nr_fragments = 0
    fragment_offsets = []
    while True:
        try:
            group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
        except Exception:
            break

        tag = group << 16 | elem
        if tag == 0xFFFEE000:
            if len(raw_length := buffer.read(4)) != 4:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Unable to determine the length of the item at offset "
                    f"{buffer.tell() - len(raw_length) - 4} as the end of "
                    "the data has been reached - the encapsulated pixel data "
                    "may be invalid"
                )
            length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", raw_length)[0]
            if length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Undefined item length at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                    "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragments"
                )
            nr_fragments += 1
            fragment_offsets.append(buffer.tell() - 8)
            buffer.seek(length, 1)
        elif tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
            break
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unexpected tag '{Tag(tag)}' at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragment items"
            )

    buffer.seek(start_offset, 0)

    return nr_fragments, fragment_offsets


def generate_fragments(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> Iterator[bytes]:
    """Yield frame fragments from the encapsulated pixel data in `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, starting at the first
        byte of item tag for a fragment, usually this will be after the end
        of the Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray` or
        an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and ``seek()`` methods. If the
        latter than the final offset position depends on how many fragments have
        been yielded.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Yields
    ------
    bytes
        A pixel data fragment.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    while True:
        try:
            group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
        except Exception:
            break

        tag = group << 16 | elem
        if tag == 0xFFFEE000:
            if len(raw_length := buffer.read(4)) != 4:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Unable to determine the length of the item at offset "
                    f"{buffer.tell() - len(raw_length) - 4} as the end of "
                    "the data has been reached - the encapsulated pixel data "
                    "may be invalid"
                )
            length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", raw_length)[0]
            if length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Undefined item length at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                    "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragments"
                )

            yield buffer.read(length)
        elif tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
            break
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unexpected tag '{Tag(tag)}' at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragment items"
            )

        * `rows`
        * `columns`
        * `bits_allocated`
        * `bits_stored`

        attr: ds[tag].value for tag, attr in _IMAGE_PIXEL.items() if tag in ds._dict

    for fragment in fragments:
        frame_fragments.append(fragment)
        if eoi_marker in fragment[-10:]:
            if frame_nr == index:
                frame = b"".join(frame_fragments)
                buffer.seek(starting_position, 0)
                return frame

            frame_nr += 1
            frame_fragments = []

    if frame_fragments and index == frame_nr:
        warn_and_log(

            "JPEG EOI/EOC marker was found, the returned frame data may be "
            "invalid"

        buffer.seek(starting_position, 0)

class _BufferedItem:
    """Convenience class for a buffered encapsulation item.

    Attributes
    ----------
    buffer : io.BufferedIOBase
        The buffer containing data to be encapsulated.
    length : int
        The total length of the encapsulated item, including the item tag and
        The total length of the encapsulated item, including the item tag and
        value and any trailing padding required to bring the item data up to an
        even length.
    """

    def __init__(self, buffer: BufferedIOBase) -> None:
        """Create a new ``_BufferedItem`` instance.

        Parameters
        ----------
        buffer : io.BufferedIOBase
            The buffer containing data to be encapsulated, may be empty.
        """
        self.buffer = buffer
        # The non-padded length of the data in the buffer
        self._blen = buffer_length(buffer)

        if self._blen > 2**32 - 2:
            raise ValueError(
                "Buffers containing more than 4294967294 bytes are not supported"
            )

        # 8 bytes for the item tag and length
        self.length = 8 + self._blen + self._blen % 2
        # Whether or not the buffer needs trailing padding
        self._padding = bool(self._blen % 2)
        # The item tag and length
        self._item = b"".join(
            (
                b"\xfe\xff\x00\xe0",
                (self.length - 8).to_bytes(length=4, byteorder="little"),
            )
        )

    def read(self, start: int, size: int) -> bytes:
        """Return data from the encapsulated frame.

        Parameters
        ----------
        start : int
            The initial position in the encapsulated item where data should be read
            from, must be greater than or equal to 0, where ``0`` is the first byte
            of the item tag.
        size : int
            The number of bytes to read from the buffer.

        Returns
        -------
        bytes
            The data read from the buffer.
        """
        if not 0 <= start < self.length:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid 'start' value '{start}', must be in the closed interval "
                f"[0, {self.length - 1}]"
            )

        nr_read = 0
        out = bytearray()
        while length := (size - nr_read):
            offset = start + nr_read
            if offset < 8:
                # `offset` in item tag/length
                _read = self._item[offset : offset + length]
            elif 0 <= (offset - 8) < self._blen:
                # `offset` in item value
                with reset_buffer_position(self.buffer):
                    self.buffer.seek(offset - 8)
                    _read = self.buffer.read(length)

            elif self._padding and offset == self.length - 1:
                # `offset` in the item value padding
                _read = b"\x00"
            else:
                # `offset` past the end of the item value
                _read = b""

            if not _read:
                break

            nr_read += len(_read)
            out.extend(_read)

        return bytes(out)


class EncapsulatedBuffer(BufferedIOBase):
    """Convenience class for managing the encapsulation of one or more buffers
    containing compressed *Pixel Data*.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0
    """

    def __init__(self, buffers: list[BufferedIOBase], use_bot: bool = False) -> None:
        """Create a new class instance.

        Parameters
        ----------
        buffers : list[io.BufferedIOBase]
            The buffered pixel data frames to be encapsulated on writing the dataset.
            Only a single frame of pixel data can be in each buffer and the buffers
            must inherit from :class:`io.BufferedIODBase` and be readable and seekable.
        use_bot : bool, optional
            If ``True`` then the Basic Offset Table will include the offsets for
            each encapsulated items, otherwise no offsets will be included (default).
        """
        if not isinstance(buffers, list):
            raise TypeError(
                "'buffers' must be a list of objects that inherit from "
                "'io.BufferedIOBase'"
            )

        self._items = [_BufferedItem(b) for b in buffers]

        # The current position of the encapsulated buffer
        self._offset = 0

        # Use a non-empty Basic Offset Table
        self._use_bot = use_bot

        # Offsets for the buffered items
        # Start of the item tag for the Basic Offset Table
        self._item_offsets = [0]
        # Start of the item tag for each frame
        self._item_offsets.extend([offset + len(bot) for offset in self.offsets])
        # End of the encapsulation
        self._item_offsets.append(self.encapsulated_length)

        # A dict containing the items to read encoded data from
        #   0: the buffered Basic Offset Table value
        #   1 to len(buffers): the buffered frames

        if not self._use_bot:

        bot = [b"\xfe\xff\x00\xe0"]
        # Add the item length
        bot.append(pack("<I", 4 * len(self.offsets)))

        bot.append(pack(f"<{len(self.offsets)}I", *self.offsets))

    @property
    def closed(self) -> bool:

        return any(item.buffer.closed for item in self._items)

    @property

    @property

        return pack(f"<{len(self.offsets)}Q", *self.offsets)

    @property
    def encapsulated_length(self) -> int:

        return len(self.basic_offset_table) + sum(self.lengths)

    def lengths(self) -> list[int]:

        return [sum(self.lengths[0:idx]) for idx, _ in enumerate(self.lengths)]

    def __deepcopy__(self, memo: dict[int, Any]) -> "Dataset":
        """Return a deep copy of the dataset.

        Makes sure that any copied private block points to the correct dataset.

        Returns
        -------
        Dataset
            A deep copy of the file dataset.
        """
        cls = self.__class__
        result = cls.__new__(cls)
        memo[id(self)] = result
        for k, v in self.__dict__.items():

                for key, block in self._private_blocks.items():

    def __delattr__(self, name: str) -> None:
        """Intercept requests to delete an attribute by `name`.

        Examples
        --------

        >>> ds = Dataset()
        >>> ds.PatientName = 'foo'
        >>> ds.some_attribute = True

        If `name` is a DICOM keyword - delete the corresponding
        :class:`~pydicom.dataelem.DataElement`

        >>> del ds.PatientName
        >>> 'PatientName' in ds
        False

        If `name` is another attribute - delete it

        >>> del ds.some_attribute
        >>> hasattr(ds, 'some_attribute')
        False

        Parameters
        ----------
        name : str
            The keyword for the DICOM element or the class attribute to delete.
        """
        # First check if a valid DICOM keyword and if we have that data element
        tag = cast(BaseTag, tag_for_keyword(name))
        if tag is not None and tag in self._dict:
            del self._dict[tag]

            # Deleting pixel data resets the stored array
            if tag in PIXEL_KEYWORDS:
                self._pixel_array = None
                self._pixel_id = {}
        # If not a DICOM name in this dataset, check for regular instance name
        #   can't do delete directly, that will call __delattr__ again
        elif name in self.__dict__:
            del self.__dict__[name]
        # Not found, raise an error in same style as python does
        else:
            raise AttributeError(name)

        >>> ds = Dataset()
        >>> ds.CommandGroupLength = 100
        >>> ds.PatientName = 'CITIZEN^Jan'
        >>> del ds[0x00000000]
        >>> ds
        (0010,0010) Patient's Name                      PN: 'CITIZEN^Jan'

        Slicing using :class:`~pydicom.dataelem.DataElement` tag

        >>> ds = Dataset()
        >>> ds.CommandGroupLength = 100
        >>> ds.SOPInstanceUID = '1.2.3'
        >>> ds.PatientName = 'CITIZEN^Jan'
        >>> del ds[:0x00100000]
        >>> ds
        (0010,0010) Patient's Name                      PN: 'CITIZEN^Jan'

        ----------
        key
            The key for the attribute to be deleted. If a ``slice`` is used
            then the tags matching the slice conditions will be deleted.

            for tag in self._slice_dataset(key.start, key.stop, key.step):

                # invalidate private blocks in case a private creator is
                # deleted - will be re-created on next access
                if self._private_blocks and BaseTag(tag).is_private_creator:

                    f"'{type(self).__name__}.save_as()' cannot be used to "
                    "convert between little and big endian encoding. Please "
                    "read the documentation for filewriter.dcmwrite() if this "
                    "is what you really want to do"
                )

        pydicom.dcmwrite(
            filename,
            self,
            __write_like_original,
            implicit_vr=implicit_vr,
            little_endian=little_endian,
            enforce_file_format=enforce_file_format,
            overwrite=overwrite,
            **kwargs,
        )

class FileMetaDataset(Dataset):
    """Contains a collection (dictionary) of group 2 DICOM Data Elements.

    .. versionadded:: 2.0

    Derived from :class:`~pydicom.dataset.Dataset`, but only allows
    Group 2 (File Meta Information) data elements
    """

    def __init__(self, *args: _DatasetType, **kwargs: Any) -> None:
        """Initialize a FileMetaDataset

        Parameters are as per :class:`Dataset`; this overrides the super class
        only to check that all are group 2 data elements

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If any data elements are not group 2.
        TypeError
            If the passed argument is not a :class:`dict` or :class:`Dataset`
        """
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        FileMetaDataset.validate(self._dict)

        # Set type hints for the possible contents - VR, Type (1|1C|3)
        self.FileMetaInformationGroupLength: int  # UL, 1
        self.FileMetaInformationVersion: bytes  # OB, 1
        self.MediaStorageSOPClassUID: UID  # UI, 1
        self.MediaStorageSOPInstanceUID: UID  # UI, 1
        self.TransferSyntaxUID: UID  # UI, 1
        self.ImplementationClassUID: UID  # UI, 1
        self.ImplementationVersionName: str | None  # SH, 3
        self.SourceApplicationEntityTitle: str | None  # AE, 3
        self.SendingApplicationEntityTitle: str | None  # AE, 3
        self.ReceivingApplicationEntityTitle: str | None  # AE, 3
        self.SourcePresentationAddress: str | None  # UR, 3
        self.ReceivingPresentationAddress: str | None  # UR, 3
        self.PrivateInformationCreatorUID: UID | None  # UI, 3
        self.PrivateInformation: bytes  # OB, 1C

    @staticmethod
    def validate(init_value: _DatasetType) -> None:
        """Raise errors if initialization value is not acceptable for file_meta

        Parameters
        ----------
        init_value: dict or Dataset
            The tag:data element pairs to initialize a file meta dataset

        Raises
        ------
        TypeError
            If the passed argument is not a :class:`dict` or :class:`Dataset`
        ValueError
            If any data elements passed are not group 2.
        """
        if init_value is None:
            return

        if not isinstance(init_value, Dataset | dict):
            raise TypeError(
                f"Argument must be a dict or Dataset, not {type(init_value)}"
            )

        non_group2 = [str(Tag(tag)) for tag in init_value.keys() if Tag(tag).group != 2]
        if non_group2:
            raise ValueError(
                "File meta datasets may only contain group 2 elements but the "
                f"following elements are present: {', '.join(non_group2)}"
            )

    def __setitem__(self, key: "slice | TagType", value: _DatasetValue) -> None:
        """Override parent class to only allow setting of group 2 elements.

        Parameters
        ----------
        key : int or Tuple[int, int] or str
            The tag for the element to be added to the Dataset.
        value : dataelem.DataElement or dataelem.RawDataElement
            The element to add to the :class:`FileMetaDataset`.

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If `key` is not a DICOM Group 2 tag.
        """

        if isinstance(value.tag, BaseTag):
            tag = value.tag
        else:
            tag = Tag(value.tag)

        if tag.group != 2:
            raise ValueError(
                "Only group 2 data elements are allowed in a FileMetaDataset"
            )

        super().__setitem__(key, value)

    @property
    def _tsyntax_encoding(self) -> tuple[bool, bool] | tuple[None, None]:
        """Return the transfer syntax encoding method (if any)

        Returns
        -------
        tuple[bool, bool] | tuple[None, None]
            If the file meta has a valid public Transfer Syntax UID then
            returns (is implicit, is little), otherwise returns (None, None).
        """
        tsyntax = self.get("TransferSyntaxUID", None)
        if not tsyntax or tsyntax.is_private or not tsyntax.is_transfer_syntax:
            return (None, None)

        return (tsyntax.is_implicit_VR, tsyntax.is_little_endian)

def add_dict_entries(
    new_entries_dict: dict[int, tuple[str, str, str, str, str]],
) -> None:
    """Update the DICOM dictionary with new non-private entries.

    Parameters
    ----------
    new_entries_dict : dict
        :class:`dict` of form:
        ``{tag: (VR, VM, description, is_retired, keyword), ...}``
        where parameters are as described in :func:`add_dict_entry`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If one of the entries is a private tag.

    See Also
    --------
    add_dict_entry
        Add a single entry to the dictionary.

    Examples
    --------

    >>> from pydicom import Dataset
    >>> new_dict_items = {
    ...        0x10021001: ('UL', '1', "Test One", '', 'TestOne'),
    ...        0x10021002: ('DS', '3', "Test Two", '', 'TestTwo'),
    ... }
    >>> add_dict_entries(new_dict_items)
    >>> ds = Dataset()
    >>> ds.TestOne = 'test'
    >>> ds.TestTwo = ['1', '2', '3']

    """

    if any([BaseTag(tag).is_private for tag in new_entries_dict]):
        raise ValueError(
            'Private tags cannot be added using "add_dict_entries" - '
            'use "add_private_dict_entries" instead'
        )

    # Update the dictionary itself
    DicomDictionary.update(new_entries_dict)

    if not all([BaseTag(tag).is_private for tag in new_entries_dict]):
        raise ValueError(
            "Non-private tags cannot be added using "
            "'add_private_dict_entries()' - use 'add_dict_entries()' instead"
        )

    new_entries = {
        f"{tag >> 16:04X}xx{tag & 0xFF:02X}": value
        for tag, value in new_entries_dict.items()
    }
    private_dictionaries.setdefault(private_creator, {}).update(new_entries)


def get_entry(tag: TagType) -> tuple[str, str, str, str, str]:
    """Return an entry from the DICOM dictionary as a tuple.

    If the `tag` is not in the main DICOM dictionary, then the repeating
    group dictionary will also be checked.

    Parameters
    ----------
    tag : int or str or Tuple[int, int]
        The tag for the element whose entry is to be retrieved, in any of the
        forms accepted by :func:`~pydicom.tag.Tag`. Only entries in the
        official DICOM dictionary will be checked, not entries in the
        private dictionary.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple of str
        The (VR, VM, name, is_retired, keyword) from the DICOM dictionary.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If the tag is not present in the DICOM data dictionary.

    See Also
    --------
    get_private_entry
        Return an entry from the private dictionary.
    """
    # Note: tried the lookup with 'if tag in DicomDictionary'
    # and with DicomDictionary.get, instead of try/except
    # Try/except was fastest using timeit if tag is valid (usual case)
    # My test had 5.2 usec vs 8.2 for 'contains' test, vs 5.32 for dict.get
    if not isinstance(tag, BaseTag):
        tag = Tag(tag)
    try:
        return DicomDictionary[tag]
    except KeyError:
        if not tag.is_private:
            mask_x = mask_match(tag)
            if mask_x:
                return RepeatersDictionary[mask_x]
        raise KeyError(f"Tag {tag} not found in DICOM dictionary")

def generate_fragments(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer, *, endianness: str = "<"
) -> Iterator[bytes]:
    """Yield frame fragments from the encapsulated pixel data in `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, starting at the first
        byte of item tag for a fragment, usually this will be after the end
        of the Basic Offset Table. May be :class:`bytes`, :class:`bytearray` or
        an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and ``seek()`` methods. If the
        latter than the final offset position depends on how many fragments have
        been yielded.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Yields
    ------
    bytes
        A pixel data fragment.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    while True:
        try:
            group, elem = unpack(f"{endianness}HH", buffer.read(4))
        except Exception:
            break

        tag = group << 16 | elem
        if tag == 0xFFFEE000:
            if len(raw_length := buffer.read(4)) != 4:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Unable to determine the length of the item at offset "
                    f"{buffer.tell() - len(raw_length) - 4} as the end of "
                    "the data has been reached - the encapsulated pixel data "
                    "may be invalid"
                )
            length = unpack(f"{endianness}L", raw_length)[0]
            if length == 0xFFFFFFFF:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Undefined item length at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                    "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragments"
                )

            yield buffer.read(length)
        elif tag == 0xFFFEE0DD:
            break
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unexpected tag '{Tag(tag)}' at offset {buffer.tell() - 4} when "
                "parsing the encapsulated pixel data fragment items"
            )


def generate_fragmented_frames(
    buffer: bytes | bytearray | ReadableBuffer,
    *,
    number_of_frames: int | None = None,
    extended_offsets: tuple[list[int], list[int]] | tuple[bytes, bytes] | None = None,
    endianness: str = "<",
) -> Iterator[tuple[bytes, ...]]:
    """Yield fragmented pixel data frames from `buffer`.

    .. versionadded:: 3.0

    .. note::

        When the Basic Offset Table is empty and the Extended Offset Table
        isn't supplied then more fragmented frames may be yielded than given
        by `number_of_frames` provided there are sufficient excess fragments
        available.

    Parameters
    ----------
    buffer : bytes | bytearray | readable buffer
        A buffer containing the encapsulated frame data, positioned at the first
        byte of the basic offset table. May be :class:`bytes`,
        :class:`bytearray` or an object with ``read()``, ``tell()`` and
        ``seek()`` methods. If the latter then the final position depends on
        how many fragmented frames have been yielded.
    number_of_frames : int, optional
        Required when the Basic Offset Table is empty and the Extended Offset Table
        has not been supplied. This should be the value of (0028,0008) *Number of
        Frames* or the expected number of frames in the encapsulated data.
    extended_offsets : tuple[list[int], list[int]] or tuple[bytes, bytes], optional
        The (offsets, lengths) of the Extended Offset Table as taken from
        (7FE0,0001) *Extended Offset Table* and (7FE0,0002) *Extended Offset
        Table Lengths* as either the raw encoded values or a list of their
        decoded equivalents.
    endianness : str, optional
        If ``"<"`` (default) then the encapsulated data uses little endian
        encoding, otherwise if ``">"`` it uses big endian encoding.

    Yields
    -------
    tuple[bytes, ...]
        An encapsulated pixel data frame, with the contents of the tuple the
        frame's fragmented encoded data.
    """
    if isinstance(buffer, bytes | bytearray):
        buffer = BytesIO(buffer)

    # `buffer` is positioned at the end of the basic offsets table

    # Prefer the extended offset table (if available)
    if extended_offsets:
        # PS3.3, C.7.6.3.1.8
        # Byte offsets to the first byte of the item tag of the first fragment
        #   of every frame, as measured from the first byte of the item tag
        #   following the Basic Offset Table, which *should* be empty
        # Only 1 fragment per frame is allowed (Table C.7-11a)
        if isinstance(extended_offsets[0], bytes):
            nr_offsets = len(extended_offsets[0]) // 8
            offsets = list(unpack(f"{endianness}{nr_offsets}Q", extended_offsets[0]))
        else:
            offsets = extended_offsets[0]

        if isinstance(extended_offsets[1], bytes):
            nr_offsets = len(extended_offsets[1]) // 8
            lengths = list(unpack(f"{endianness}{nr_offsets}Q", extended_offsets[1]))
        else:
            lengths = extended_offsets[1]

        fragments_start = buffer.tell()
        for offset, length in zip(offsets, lengths):
            # 8 for the item tag and item length, which we don't need
            buffer.seek(fragments_start + offset + 8, 0)
            yield (buffer.read(length),)

        return

    # Fall back to the basic offset table (if available)
    if basic_offsets:
        frame = []
        current_index = 0
        current_offset = 0
        final_index = len(basic_offsets) - 1
        for fragment in generate_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness):
            if current_index == final_index:
                # Nth frame, keep adding fragments until we have no more
                frame.append(fragment)
                continue

            if current_offset < basic_offsets[current_index + 1]:
                # N - 1th frame, keep adding fragments until the we go
                #   past the next frame offset
                frame.append(fragment)
            else:
                # Gone past the next offset, yield and restart
                yield tuple(frame)
                current_index += 1
                frame = [fragment]

            # + 8 bytes for item tag and item length
            current_offset += len(fragment) + 8

        # Yield the Nth frame
        yield tuple(frame)
        return

    # No basic or extended offset table
    # Determine the number of fragments in the buffer
    nr_fragments, _ = parse_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness)
    # `buffer` is positioned at the end of the basic offsets table
    fragments = generate_fragments(buffer, endianness=endianness)

    # Single fragment must be 1 frame
    if nr_fragments == 1:
        yield (next(fragments),)
        return

    # From this point on we require the number of frames as there are
    #   multiple fragments and may be one or more frames
    if not number_of_frames:
        raise ValueError(
            "Unable to determine the frame boundaries for the encapsulated "
            "pixel data as there is no Basic or Extended Offset Table and "
            "the number of frames has not been supplied"
        )

    # 1 fragment per frame, for N frames
    if nr_fragments == number_of_frames:
        # Covers RLE and others if 1:1 ratio
        yield from ((fragment,) for fragment in fragments)
        return

    # Multiple fragments for 1 frame
    if number_of_frames == 1:
        yield tuple(fragment for fragment in fragments)
        return

    # More fragments then frames
    if nr_fragments > number_of_frames:
        # Search for JPEG/JPEG-LS/JPEG2K EOI/EOC marker which should be the
        #   last two bytes of a frame
        # It's possible to yield more frames than `number_of_frames` as
        #   long as there are excess fragments with JPEG EOI/EOC markers
        # It's also possible that we yielded too early because the marker bytes
        #   were actually part of the compressed JPEG codestream
        eoi_marker = b"\xff\xd9"

        frame_nr = 0
        for fragment in fragments:
            frame.append(fragment)
            if eoi_marker in fragment[-10:]:
                yield tuple(frame)
                frame_nr += 1
                frame = []

        # There was a final set of fragments with no EOI/EOC marker, data is
        #   probably corrupted, but yield it and warn/log anyway
        if frame:
            if frame_nr >= number_of_frames:

                    "The end of the encapsulated pixel data has been reached but "
                    "no JPEG EOI/EOC marker was found, the final frame may be "
                    "be invalid"
                )
            else:
                msg = (
                    "The end of the encapsulated pixel data has been reached but "
                    "fewer frames than expected have been found. Please confirm "
                    "that the generated frame data is correct"
                )

            warn_and_log(msg)
            yield tuple(frame)

        elif frame_nr < number_of_frames:
            warn_and_log(
                "The end of the encapsulated pixel data has been reached but "
                "fewer frames than expected have been found"
            )

        return

    # nr_fragments < number_of_frames
    raise ValueError(
        "Unable to generate frames from the encapsulated pixel data as there "
        "are fewer fragments than frames; the dataset may be corrupt or the "
        "number of frames may be incorrect"
    )
